summary: Round-2 re-review confirms the single round-1 minor finding is fully addressed. The fix commit 8ceec6c touches ProjectHardDeleteJob.java with comment-only changes (verified byte-level: zero non-comment production line changes vs parent) — the GRIDFS_FILES_COLLECTION constant now documents the bucket-sync requirement, and the cascade block now documents the advisory pre-delete count and the accepted non-transactional orphan-chunk window. Cascade logic, ordering, log shape, and null-defensive DeleteResult handling are unchanged from the round-1 approved state. Test reworks (genuine partial-drain recovery test, new GridFS-orphan sweep test, deterministic AtomicLong seeds) do not affect production correctness and strengthen coverage; both ITs run green (12 + 3 = 15 tests, 0 failures/0 errors on a forced --rerun-tasks).

round1FindingsResolution.round1Issue: fs.files hardcoded as default bucket name; count read (template.count on literal) and delete (gridFsOperations.delete, honors configured bucket) are decoupled — a future custom bucket would silently break the count metric.
round1FindingsResolution.evidence: Lines 39-41: the constant comment now states 'Must stay in sync with the GridFS bucket the delete targets — no custom bucket is configured, so the default holds.' Lines 109-112: the cascade comment now explicitly frames the count as 'an advisory pre-delete snapshot for the log line, not a transactional erasure receipt — the delete re-runs the query independently, so erasure is correct even if the count drifts.' This was a count/observability coupling (not a correctness bug), and documenting the invariant is the appropriate resolution. No code change was required or made.

regressionChecks.detail: git diff 8ceec6c~1..8ceec6c on ProjectHardDeleteJob.java filtered to non-comment/non-blank lines yields zero hits. Cascade order (events -> GridFS -> subscriber_exports -> subscriber_events -> subscribers -> tags -> emit project_hard_deleted -> drop projects), the +1ns cutoff, the zero-deletion short-circuit, null-defensive removeByProjectId, and both INFO log shapes are identical to the round-1 approved version.

cron_cascadeRecoversPartialDrainThenSecondRunIsNoOp now models a real partial-cascade crash: project still soft-deleted, subscribers pre-drained (not seeded), tags/subscriber_events/subscriber_exports/GridFS survive. Asserted log line deletedCount=1 eventsRemovedCount=0 gridFsFilesRemoved=1 exportsRemoved=1 subscriberEventsRemoved=1 subscribersRemoved=0 tagsRemoved=1 is consistent with the seed (no events seeded -> 0; the run-emitted project_hard_deleted row lands AFTER the sweep so is not counted; subscribers never seeded -> 0; four survivors -> 1 each). The second-run no-op uses countOccurrences on the all-zero substring and expects exactly 1 — correct, since only the second run emits an all-zero line.

cron_gridFsFileWithoutExportPointer_isStillSwept seeds a GridFS blob with metadata.projectId but no subscriber_exports pointer row, then asserts the blob is swept. This locks in the GridFS-keyed-by-metadata.projectId / GridFS-before-exports contract (Decision 8) without altering production behavior. gridFsFileExists helper uses gridFsOperations.findOne(metadata.projectId is ...) — matches the production delete criterion.

System.nanoTime() seeds replaced with a static AtomicLong SEQ for the unique-compound fields (subscribers (projectId,telegramUserId), tags (projectId,slug)). Removes a latent flaky-seed risk on platforms where nanoTime is not distinct across rapid consecutive calls. Test-only. (seedSubscriberEvent still uses nanoTime for subscriberId, but that field carries no unique index, so collisions are harmless.)

New helpers countByProjectId(Class,String), gridFsFileExists(String), and countOccurrences(String,String) are all defined in the IT and used consistently. AtomicLong import added. SubscriberExport status DONE is correctly documented as load-bearing for the (projectId) partial-unique index that only covers in-flight (PENDING/RUNNING) exports.
